PURPOSE.statement: Correct three FIBDB-052 index dispositions that were frozen without the measurement the same authority applied elsewhere, correct the evidence anchor whose measurement population was inconsistent with that same rule, and re-derive every count that depends on either. Nothing else is reopened.
what_this_is: A docs-only, append-only successor authority correcting dispositions inside an integrated amendment.
The successor whose absence caused the integrated audit to withhold FIBIU-19 P1 implementation authorization.
A re-freeze of the FIBDB-052 disposition partition and its dependent arithmetic.
what_this_is_not: NOT an implementation of FIBDB-052 or any phase of it. No DDL is written, authorized or scheduled by this artifact.
NOT a migration. No db/migrations/** file is created, and no migration ordinal is allocated, reserved or implied.
NOT a lineage allocation. No ODS addendum ordinal, no HPO grant, no scope allowlist row and no Controller enumeration is allocated, reserved or implied.
NOT a retraction of v1.0.1. The integrated amendment stands; its exact-object delivery was already audited PASS and is not disturbed.
NOT an authorization to drop any existing index. See ADDITIONAL_FINDINGS.
NOT a reopening of the STAGED decision, the G2 boundaries, the FIBDB-053 protections, the HPO ratification, the 24 reason-code contract or the manifest disposition.

M-1.claim: The PR118 post-integration audit artifact is integrated and readable at AS_OF_HEAD.

M-2.claim: Each of the three relations carries a UNIQUE constraint over exactly the column list its proposed index would have created, and each constraint was created once and never dropped.
measurement: A grep for DROP CONSTRAINT across db/migrations/*.sql restricted to the three relations returns no match. The three constraint identifiers appear in the migration corpus exactly once each: at their point of creation.

M-3.claim: All three UNIQUE constraints are live at the current schema snapshot with exactly those column lists in exactly that order.
M-3.measurement: db/migrations/meta/0067_snapshot.json, uniqueConstraints: domain_object_versions_object_ordinal_unique -> [object_type, object_id, ordinal]; evidence_versions_evidence_ordinal_unique -> [evidence_id, ordinal]; financial_proxy_versions_proxy_ordinal_unique -> [financial_proxy_id, ordinal]. Column ORDER is preserved by the snapshot and matches the proposed leading-column order in all three cases.

M-4.claim: Every column covered by the three constraints is NOT NULL, which closes the only semantic gap a UNIQUE index could have had against a plain index over the same columns.
M-4.measurement: 0067_snapshot.json columns: object_type varchar(100) notNull=true, object_id uuid notNull=true, ordinal integer notNull=true; evidence_id uuid notNull=true, ordinal integer notNull=true; financial_proxy_id uuid notNull=true, ordinal integer notNull=true. All three constraints carry nullsNotDistinct=false.
M-4.why_this_matters: nullsNotDistinct=false means the constraint treats NULLs as distinct, which in the general case is a real difference in the tuple space a UNIQUE index constrains. Because every constrained column is NOT NULL, that difference is unreachable: no row can carry a NULL in any covered column, so the constraint-backed btree indexes exactly the tuple space a plain index over the same columns would index. The discharge does not rest on tolerating a gap; it rests on the gap being unreachable.
M-4.status: EXTENDS - this measurement was not performed by the source audit.

M-5.claim: A PostgreSQL UNIQUE table constraint is implemented by an automatically created unique btree index over exactly those columns in that order, and a btree index supports backward scans, so an index recorded ASC serves DESC ordering over the same column list.
M-5.measurement: NOT a new machine measurement by this docs-only mission. This is the SAME derived semantic that v1.0.1 asserts at evidence anchor B10 and relies upon to discharge I-16 against FIBDB-022 and I-18 against FIBDB-050. This artifact applies that rule consistently rather than introducing it.
M-5.status: DERIVED - carried as an implementation-time verification obligation, see CORRECTED_VERIFICATION_OBLIGATION. It is not asserted as a machine fact by this mission.

RETIRED_CREATE_TARGET_NAMES.rule: These three rule-derived names were CREATE targets in v1.0.1 and are NOT CREATE targets under this authority. They name nothing that exists and nothing that may be created. No index may be created under any of them.
RETIRED_CREATE_TARGET_NAMES.why_recorded_rather_than_deleted: B20 holds that CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS resolves on the index NAME, not on its DEFINITION. A retired name is therefore not inert: an implementing mission that re-derived it from INDEX_NAMING_RULE without reading this correction would create three duplicate indexes and the IF NOT EXISTS guard would not stop it. Recording the retired names makes their retirement legible instead of leaving it as an absence.

anchor_count_derivation.why_not_22: The B18 correction was deliberately NOT issued as a second anchor. Correcting B18 in place keeps the citation chain intact - INDEX_NAMING_RULE and the length self-checks cite B18 by name - and leaves exactly one live claim per fact.

CORRECTED_VERIFICATION_OBLIGATION.rule: v1.0.1's F-A6 carries B20's name-based IF NOT EXISTS semantics as an implementation-time verification obligation covering I-11, I-16 and I-18. That obligation is WIDENED to cover all six items whose discharge depends on an object that already exists.
CORRECTED_VERIFICATION_OBLIGATION.coverage_composition: 4 items whose governed_index_name names an existing object directly (I-1, I-2, I-4, I-11) plus 2 items discharged by an owning object's constraint without naming an index themselves (I-16, I-18).
CORRECTED_VERIFICATION_OBLIGATION.the_obligation: Before discharging any of these six items, the implementing mission MUST verify against the live database that the named existing object - or, for I-16 and I-18, the owning object's constraint and its backing unique index - is present, covers exactly the stated columns in the stated order, and is unchanged. It MUST NOT emit CREATE INDEX for any of the six. It MUST NOT emit CREATE INDEX under any name in RETIRED_CREATE_TARGET_NAMES.
CORRECTED_VERIFICATION_OBLIGATION.why_this_is_load_bearing: B20 holds that CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS resolves on the index NAME, not on the index DEFINITION. For all six items a definitionally equivalent index already exists under a name the rule-derived scheme would not produce. IF NOT EXISTS therefore provides NO protection: emitting the rule-derived name would silently create a permanent duplicate rather than being inert.
CORRECTED_VERIFICATION_OBLIGATION.epistemic_status_preserved: B20's name-based matching remains DERIVED, not machine-proven by any docs-only mission. LANE BL machine-proved that a name is REQUIRED; it did not machine-prove name-based rather than definition-based matching, and neither this mission nor v1.0.1 executed DDL. The conservative disposition is chosen in all six cases - verify, do not emit - so if the semantics were somehow otherwise, the result is a no-op rather than a wrong index.
CORRECTED_VERIFICATION_OBLIGATION.owner: The FIBDB-052/P1, P3 and P5 implementing missions.

ADDITIONAL_FINDINGS.rule: Observational only. Nothing in this section is DDL authority, and nothing here authorizes dropping, altering or replacing any existing object.

F-GC-1.finding: Three standalone indexes are strict leading prefixes of the constraint-backed UNIQUE indexes that now discharge I-1, I-2 and I-4: idx_domain_object_versions_object over (object_type, object_id) is a strict leading prefix of domain_object_versions_object_ordinal_unique over (object_type, object_id, ordinal); idx_evidence_versions_evidence_id over (evidence_id) is a strict leading prefix of evidence_versions_evidence_ordinal_unique over (evidence_id, ordinal); idx_financial_proxy_versions_proxy_id over (financial_proxy_id) is a strict leading prefix of financial_proxy_versions_proxy_ordinal_unique over (financial_proxy_id, ordinal).
F-GC-1.how_measured: Column lists read from db/migrations/meta/0067_snapshot.json for both the declared index and the unique constraint on each of the three relations, and cross-checked against the CREATE INDEX statements at 0045:52, 0048:53 and 0053:99.
F-GC-1.consequence_if_true: Each prefix index is redundant for lookup, since a btree over (a, b) serves any query a btree over (a) serves. The cost is write amplification and storage, never correctness. No query returns a different result.
F-GC-1.DISPOSITION: OBSERVED. NOT ACTIONED. NO DROP IS AUTHORIZED. Dropping an existing index is a behavioural change on a live surface and is outside this docs-only mission's authority. Recorded as a redundancy CANDIDATE so a future mission holding the appropriate authority decides deliberately rather than inheriting the redundancy unnoticed.
